To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have synthesized fouling-resistant and electrically conductive zwitterionic poly(3,3’-(ethylenediooxy)bis(2-(3-(trimethoxysilyl)propylthiophene-5-ylidene)malononitrile)) (PEDTz) coatings via oxidative chemical vapor depostion.

zwitterionic PEDOT (z-PEDOT) coatings, which are prepared via oxidative chemical vapor depositions, are fouling resistant, electrically conductive, and thin (ca. 100 nm) and can be used for a range of applications, including the self-cleaning of membranes, bioelectronics, and the fouling of other surfaces.
we have synthesized fouling-resistant and conductive polymeric coatings via chemical vapor deposition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of multifunctionally fouling-resistant and electrically conductive coatings for the electrolysis-based cleaning of fouled surfaces.
the synthesis of fouling-resistant, thin, and conductive films via a novel oCVD process.
the development of a novel multifunctional thin film with fouling resistance and conductive properties for their potential applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

oCVD-derived zwitterionic coatings have superior fouling resistance to gold, PDMS, and the other fouling-resistant coatings tested, and that the oCVD-derived coatings also exhibit conductivity, making them multifunctional and potentially useful for a wide range of applications.
the fouling resistance and conductivity of the PEDOT-based coatings are both excellent, and that the PEDOT-based coating exhibits the best overall combination of these two important properties.
the oCVD-derived PEDOT coatings are fouling-resistant, conductive, and have the potential for use in a variety of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we were successful in synthesizing fouling-resistant and conductive coatings via oxidative CVD, and we demonstrated that these coatings have the potential to be applied to electrolysis-based self-cleanable separation membranes.
we report a multifunctional surface that is conductive, fouling-resistant, and has a low surface energy.
the oCVD of PEDOT is a versatile and facile method to deposit thin, fouling-resistant, and conductive films on various substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fouling-resistant coatings with electrical conductivity can be achieved by oCVD.

fouling-resistant surfaces with high conductivity can be synthesized via oCVD of PEDOT derivatives, and these surfaces are suitable for use in applications such as the electrolysis-based cleaning of membranes and in bioelectronics.
fouling-resistant coatings with electrical conductivity can be synthesized via oCVD.
